scenes.title: Separate kinds of commitment
scenes.narration: Interest, giving time, taking a trial action, stating a price preference and making a payment are different signals. A stronger-looking signal still needs its context and limits. Do not treat a sign-up or compliment as a purchase.

scenes.title: Choose one assumption
scenes.narration: State the offer and one assumption you want to explore. Ask who decides, who uses it and what the current alternative is. A hypothetical price answer is reported preference, not a payment or a forecast of revenue.

scenes.title: Explain the offer honestly
scenes.narration: Explain what exists, what is proposed and what would be delivered. Make participation voluntary. Do not invent scarcity, hide manual work or imply a service is available when it is not.

scenes.title: Plan a bounded check
scenes.narration: A voluntary scheduled demo may explore a time commitment; record accepted, scheduled, attended or cancelled separately. It does not establish payment. If exploring price language, use neutral questions and preserve hypothetical status.

scenes.title: Keep payments separate
scenes.narration: This lesson collects no money. Any future real payment test needs reviewed offer terms, delivery capability, payment handling and refund or cancellation arrangements before it begins. Do not take payment for an undefined or unfulfillable promise.

scenes.title: Write the brief
scenes.narration: Create your Commitment and Payment Assumption Brief with claim, honest terms, method, evidence rule and safeguards. If no test ran, write not run. Rehearsal is practice. One action or purchase does not prove repeated demand, retention or sustainable revenue.

sections.label: 02 / LEARN
sections.heading: Name the commitment before interpreting it.

children: A
commitment
is a specific action or obligation someone agrees to.
Stated price preference
is what they say about a hypothetical price.
Actual payment
requires a real verified transaction under a defined offer; this prototype processes none.
Different signals
Compliment: reported interest.
Demo accepted: stated agreement.
Demo attended: observed time commitment.
Trial task completed: bounded task action.
Hypothetical price answer: stated preference.
Keep limits visible
Attendance does not prove purchase. A purchase under one offer does not prove retention or sustainable revenue. Context, delivery, incentives and cancellations matter.
Specify customer, user/decision-maker context and offer.
Choose one claim and the exact commitment you will request.
Disclose proposed versus available capabilities and any obligations.
Use a neutral, voluntary request with no pressure or false scarcity.
Record the actual status and source; keep intention and action separate.
Set a review rule, stop conditions and safeguards before testing.
Illustrative planned check — no outreach sent

Claim: relevant adults will give time to explore a clearly labeled registration concept. Request: an optional 15-minute concept demo through an approved route. Record invited, accepted, scheduled, attended or cancelled distinctly. Attendance supports a bounded time-commitment claim only; payment remains unknown. Access pending, no test run.

When exploring price language, ask neutrally about the current alternative and decision context. Do not insert hypothetical answers into revenue projections as verified purchases. Incentives tied to participation may affect the signal; disclose and record them. Never reward only positive feedback.

This lesson designs a check and collects no money. Before any future actual payment test, the responsible owners must review deliverable scope, availability, terms, payment handling and refund/cancellation arrangements. Do not use an undefined or unfulfillable offer. Use anonymous planning notes here; no contact details or payment data.
Review measurement plan
